footer.mission: A pan-African community where founders build, pitch, get challenged and grow.

hero.body: Africa Founders Factory is a community where entrepreneurs challenge their ideas, sharpen their pitch, strengthen their ventures and connect with people who can help them move forward.

problem.body: Most founders don't lack ambition. They lack the pressure-testing, storytelling and access that turn a promising idea into a venture people believe in.

items.title: Unclear Positioning
items.body: A founder may understand the idea deeply while the market still doesn't understand why it matters.

items.title: Weak Storytelling
items.body: A good business badly explained can look like a bad business.

items.title: Lack of Challenge
items.body: Without external feedback, assumptions easily become convictions.

items.title: Limited Access
items.body: Talent is everywhere. Access to experienced people isn't.

sentences: Every founder starts with a rough idea worth pressure-testing.
Sharpen the story until it is impossible to misunderstand.
Turn the idea into something real people can react to.
Say it out loud, in front of people who will push back.
Face direct, expert scrutiny of the venture and the story.
Take the feedback and rebuild the weak parts.
Meet the people who can open the next door.
Keep moving, one iteration at a time.

mission.body1: Africa Founders Factory is a pan-African community built around one loop: build, pitch, get challenged, improve, connect, grow. There are no paid plans, no consulting packages and no fundraising promises today — only a place where founders can pressure-test their ideas against real people who understand the journey.
mission.body2: We believe the biggest constraint on African founders isn't a shortage of ideas — it's the lack of structured challenge, storytelling practice and access to experienced people that turns a promising idea into a venture people believe in.

about.headline: A pan-African community, built community-first.
about.body1: Africa Founders Factory is starting as a community: founders, aspiring founders, experts, mentors, operators, diaspora and ecosystem partners, gathering around one loop — build, pitch, get challenged, improve, connect, grow.
about.body2: There are no paid plans, consulting packages or subscriptions today. Advanced programs may come later, once the community and the Factory model are proven together.

questions.q_product_validation: Have you validated your product with real users beyond friends and family?
questions.q_technical_feasibility: How technically de-risked is your product today?
questions.q_product_roadmap: Do you have a clear product roadmap for the next two quarters?
questions.q_execution_capacity: How would you rate your team's ability to execute against your plan?
questions.q_domain_expertise: Do you or a co-founder have direct prior experience in this industry?
questions.q_team_governance: Do you have a clear decision-making process among founders (defined roles, regular syncs)?
questions.q_revenue_consistency: Is your revenue mostly recurring or one-off?
questions.q_forecasting: Do you maintain an updated financial forecast or model?
questions.q_fundraising_readiness: Do you have an up-to-date pitch deck and financial model ready to share with investors?
questions.q_operational_processes: Do you have documented operating processes (onboarding, delivery, support)?
questions.q_delivery_capacity: How confident are you in delivering at 2x your current volume without breaking?
questions.q_tooling_and_systems: Do you use dedicated tools or systems to run daily operations (CRM, accounting, support)?
questions.q_scalability_readiness: How scalable is your current operating model?

validate_market_evidence.title: Validate your market with real evidence
validate_market_evidence.description: Gather concrete evidence — customer interviews, survey data, or market research — that confirms the problem you're solving is real and widespread.
validate_market_evidence.evidenceRequirement: At least 10 documented customer interviews or a market study with sourced data.
validate_market_evidence.task1: Interview 10 target customers about the problem
validate_market_evidence.task2: Summarize findings into a one-page market evidence brief

competitive_landscape_map.title: Map your competitive landscape
competitive_landscape_map.description: Identify direct and indirect competitors and articulate how your approach compares.
competitive_landscape_map.evidenceRequirement: A competitor comparison covering at least 3 alternatives.

run_product_validation.title: Run a structured product validation
run_product_validation.description: Test your current product with real users and capture structured feedback before investing further in build.
run_product_validation.evidenceRequirement: Documented usability/validation sessions with at least 5 users.
run_product_validation.task1: Run validation sessions with 5 target users
run_product_validation.task2: Document key findings and next steps

clarify_differentiation.title: Clarify your differentiation
clarify_differentiation.description: Write a clear, specific statement of what makes your product different from alternatives, and why that matters to customers.
clarify_differentiation.evidenceRequirement: A one-paragraph differentiation statement reviewed by a founder.

define_unit_economics.title: Define your unit economics
define_unit_economics.description: Calculate the core unit economics of your business — cost to acquire, cost to serve, and revenue per unit — so profitability is measurable.
define_unit_economics.evidenceRequirement: A documented unit economics model (CAC, margin, LTV where applicable).
define_unit_economics.task1: Calculate cost to acquire and cost to serve per unit

define_pricing.title: Define your pricing
define_pricing.description: Set a clear, documented pricing structure aligned to the value you deliver.
define_pricing.evidenceRequirement: A documented pricing structure with at least one tier.
define_pricing.task1: Draft and document your pricing structure

measure_retention.title: Start measuring retention
measure_retention.description: Put a simple, repeatable retention measurement in place so you know whether customers keep using or buying from you.
measure_retention.evidenceRequirement: At least one retention metric (e.g. month-2 retention) tracked over two periods.
measure_retention.task1: Define and start tracking a retention metric
measure_retention.task2: Review retention after the first measurement period

track_growth_metrics.title: Track your growth metrics
track_growth_metrics.description: Put a lightweight dashboard in place tracking your core growth metric period over period.
track_growth_metrics.evidenceRequirement: A growth metric tracked for at least two consecutive periods.
track_growth_metrics.task1: Set up a simple growth metrics tracker

fill_key_roles.title: Fill your key missing roles
fill_key_roles.description: Identify the roles most critical to your next milestone that are currently unfilled, and build a plan to fill them.
fill_key_roles.evidenceRequirement: A documented org plan naming the key roles and a hiring or co-founder plan.
fill_key_roles.task1: List the key roles missing from your team
fill_key_roles.task2: Draft a plan to fill the highest-priority role

formalize_governance.title: Formalize your governance structure
formalize_governance.description: Put basic governance practices in place — regular founder/board check-ins and documented decision rights.
formalize_governance.evidenceRequirement: Documented governance cadence and decision-making process.
formalize_governance.task1: Document your governance cadence and decision rights

build_financial_forecast.title: Build a 12-month financial forecast
build_financial_forecast.description: Create a 12-month forecast covering revenue, costs, and cash position so you can plan runway and fundraising with confidence.
build_financial_forecast.task1: Build a 12-month revenue and cost forecast
build_financial_forecast.task2: Review the forecast against actuals monthly

improve_burn_control.title: Improve burn control
improve_burn_control.description: Review your monthly burn rate and put a lightweight process in place to keep it aligned with your runway target.
improve_burn_control.evidenceRequirement: A documented monthly burn review process.
improve_burn_control.task1: Review last 3 months of burn against runway target

clarify_use_of_funds.title: Clarify your use of funds
clarify_use_of_funds.description: Write a clear, specific breakdown of how you would deploy new funding across the next 12-18 months.
clarify_use_of_funds.evidenceRequirement: A documented use-of-funds breakdown by category.

prepare_investor_materials.title: Prepare your investor materials
prepare_investor_materials.description: Assemble the core materials investors expect — a pitch deck and a data room — so you're ready to engage when the time comes.
prepare_investor_materials.evidenceRequirement: A pitch deck and a data room with core documents uploaded.
prepare_investor_materials.task1: Draft or update your pitch deck
prepare_investor_materials.task2: Assemble your data room's core documents

adopt_core_tooling.title: Adopt core operating tooling
adopt_core_tooling.description: Put the essential tools in place (e.g. CRM, project tracking, accounting) to run your operations reliably as you grow.
adopt_core_tooling.evidenceRequirement: Core operating tools identified and adopted.
adopt_core_tooling.task1: Identify and adopt your core operating tools

plan_scalability.title: Plan for scalability
plan_scalability.description: Identify the operational bottlenecks that would break under 5-10x growth, and outline how you'd address them.
plan_scalability.evidenceRequirement: A documented list of scaling bottlenecks and mitigation plan.
plan_scalability.task1: List your top scaling bottlenecks and mitigations

formalize_legal_entity.title: Formalize your legal entity
formalize_legal_entity.description: Confirm your legal entity is properly formed and structured for your current stage and jurisdiction.
formalize_legal_entity.task1: Confirm or complete legal entity formation

standardize_contracts.title: Standardize your contracts and agreements
standardize_contracts.description: Put standard templates in place for the agreements you use most (customer, vendor, employment/contractor).
standardize_contracts.evidenceRequirement: Standard contract templates in place for your most common agreement types.
standardize_contracts.task1: Adopt standard templates for your most common agreements

track_impact_metrics.title: Start tracking impact metrics
track_impact_metrics.description: Define and start tracking the 2-3 metrics that best represent the impact you aim to create.
track_impact_metrics.evidenceRequirement: At least one impact metric tracked over one reporting period.
track_impact_metrics.task1: Define and start tracking your core impact metric

collect_beneficiary_evidence.title: Collect beneficiary evidence
collect_beneficiary_evidence.description: Gather direct evidence — testimonials, surveys, or data — from the people your product is meant to benefit.
collect_beneficiary_evidence.evidenceRequirement: At least 5 documented pieces of beneficiary feedback or evidence.
collect_beneficiary_evidence.task1: Collect feedback or evidence from 5 beneficiaries

hook.title: Hook / Intro
hook.guidance: Open with one sharp sentence that makes the audience lean in — the stakes, not the company history.

problem.title: Problem
problem.guidance: Explain who suffers, how badly, and why existing alternatives fail them. Evidence beats adjectives.

solution.title: Solution
solution.guidance: State what you built and why it solves the problem better than alternatives — one clear idea, not a feature list.

product.title: Product
product.guidance: Describe how the product actually works and what stage it's at (concept, MVP, live).

market.title: Market
market.guidance: Size the opportunity and name the customer segments you're targeting — grounded numbers, not "huge market" claims.

business_model.title: Business Model
business_model.guidance: Explain how you make money: pricing, revenue streams, and who pays.

traction.title: Traction
traction.guidance: Show real evidence of progress — metrics with sources, not general claims of momentum.

competition.title: Competition
competition.guidance: Name real alternatives and explain your durable advantage, not just a feature comparison.

go_to_market.title: Go-to-Market
go_to_market.guidance: Explain how you'll reach and acquire customers at scale.

team.title: Team
team.guidance: Show why this team is the right one to execute — relevant experience, not just titles.

financials.title: Financials
financials.guidance: Summarize revenue, burn and runway — the numbers investors will ask for anyway.

fundraising_ask.title: Fundraising / Ask
fundraising_ask.guidance: State the amount, instrument and what it unlocks — a specific, answerable ask.

vision_impact.title: Vision / Impact
vision_impact.guidance: Paint where this goes in 5 years, and the impact it creates beyond revenue.

closing.title: Closing
closing.guidance: End with a clear, memorable call to action.
